pr_title: net: websockets: Fix websocket close procedure
pr_body:
The websocket implementation did not comply with the RFC 6455 when it
comes to connection close. The websocket should send in such case Close
control frame, and wait for the reply, before closing the underlying TCP
connection. This commit fixes this behaviour.

Additionally, fix a small mutext-related bug with websockets.

Fixes #53942
pr_comments:
> I took a quick look on the existing websocket test. I do not understand how the sockets are created @jukkar. Do you know how this should work?

The websocket tests are implemented "slightly" hackish way. It would have required lot ot extra code to implement the websocket server for the unit tests (we have the websocket client support in zephyr). Because of this, we have a check in `websocket_send_msg()` for `CONFIG_NET_TEST` which bypasses various checks and allows us to run the unit tests without actually needing to run the connect function and connect to a websocket server. Of course it would be best if we could have a simple websocket server implementation, patches are welcome of course. 

For a true network e2e tests for websocket, it could also be possible to utilize the net e2e network tests described here https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/scripts/net/README.txt. 
I managed to implement many of those and they are tracked in #29764, unfortunately the websocket_client sample is not one of the implemented test. Perhaps it could be a better idea to improve the net e2e tests for websocket and keep the unit test a simple one. Not sure about the current net e2e test status, but I suspect that no one has been running those network e2e tests and the tests might have been bit rotted atm.

> What happens if the other side initiates the close?

The Zephyr websocket client impelmentation does not handle control frames (hell, till recently they were not even process correctly). So it's up to the application right now to check if the close message was received and act accordingly.

I don't think that this is great, and IMO the websocket code should take care of dealing with control frames like close, ping etc. However  I don't think this is in the scope of this PR.

> The Zephyr websocket client impelmentation does not handle control frames (hell, till recently they were not even process correctly). So it's up to the application right now to check if the close message was received and act accordingly.

For the client to be able to handle this situation correctly, upon reception of a close event, it must be able to send a close reply. Next it must also be able to close the websocket without sending the close message.
The suggested implementation does not offer this option.

> > > What happens if the other side initiates the close?

Why not? Upon receiving the close control frame, the client would simply close the websocket "socket" (or call `websocket_disconnect()`). The websocket code will send a close message on the client behalf, and wait for the server to close the underlying connection. According to RFC, it's server responsibility to close the TCP connection:
> The server MUST close the underlying TCP
   connection immediately; the client SHOULD wait for the server to
   close the connection but MAY close the connection at any time after
   sending and receiving a Close message, e.g., if it has not received a
   TCP Close from the server in a reasonable time period.

Note that there's no differentiation beween close request/response, it's just a close control frame, having the same format in both cases.

ret = websocket_recv_msg(ctx->sock, &buf, sizeof(buf),

Will return because the connection had been closed. Sound like a workable solution.

> and wait for the server to close the underlying connection

Yes, and this is what I am worried about. As the connection is basically closed now, why would we need to wait the server to send us anything after the connection is closed. The websocket lib has basically worked like that already, only thing missing was the sending of the close message. From server point of view it has received the close message and should be happy now. You mentioned in the issue that many of the servers do not close the connection according to the spec. So it should do no harm if we are a bit faster with the connection closing. If the server sends us a close ack back, then this patch is good, but if it does not (could happen if the server has not implemented this properly), then we just have extra 2 sec timeout without any extra benefit as the socket is basically closed already for both parties.
I am proposing here that we send the close message, but then do not wait anything back but just proceed with socket closing.

issue_context.title: Websocket: No close message on websocket close
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When a websocket is being closed, it is expected to send a message of WEBSOCKET_FLAG_CLOSE. Although this implementations just closes the TCP connection without sending a websocket message with the flag WEBSOCKET_FLAG_CLOSE. The result is that other implementations observe an unexpected websocket close error.


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Build an websocket application
2. Build up a connection to a websocket server
3. Do some data transfer
4. Call a close on the websocket
5. See the server create an exception of an unexpected websocket close

**Expected behavior**
The websocket is properly closed, no error by the websocket server.
comments:
@ssharks Please give https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/54141 a try.

Funnily, it was actually not that easy to find a peer to test that would actually respect the RFC in terms of close procedure. Python websocket server did not reply with `close` packet, MQTT mosquitto behaved the same way as Zephyr, closing the underlying connection as soon as MQTT disconnect was received.

review_comments: The return code is overwritten by the close here, is this intended?
Yes, IMO `close()` is essential here when it comes to the error code returned, as send could fail in certain cases (for example if the peer has already closed the TCP connection).
